findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no Certified Food Protection Manager present during today’s inspection. Educated PIC that there needs to be a certified food protection manager during operation hours at all times. Ensure that a certified food protection manager is present at the facility during operational hours.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was no sanitizer in sani bucket during today’s inspection. Education was carried out. PIC made the sanitizer for the sani bucket and placed it in the serving area. Ensure that there is always sanitizer in the sani bucket during food prep and handling at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The nozzles on the soda machine were observed to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. PIC removed the nozzles, cleaned and sanitized them while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

PIC  assured inspector that the three compartment sink will be sealed to the wall properly. Ensure that the caulking is redone providing a smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training for the other employee present. The employee confirmed that they had not done the food handler training hence that lack of certification. Education was carried out. Inspector will return on 5/21/26 to followup on food handler certification. Ensure that every employee receives and completes food handler training before handling any food at all times or 30-days after their employment. 


410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The back entrance of the facility has visible light gaps present when the door is closed.  These gaps allow for the entrance of insects and other pests. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the necessary repairs will be done.  Ensure that repairs are made to protect the outer opening of the establishment from pests entry.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a mop head being stored on the floor in the utility sink. Discussed with PIC and the mop storage was corrected. Ensure that mop head is stored properly to allow it to air dry to avoid the growth of bacteria culture and pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following locations were observed to have an accumulation of food debris/soils that will need to be cleaned and sanitized:
-The magnetic knife holder is observed with food debris/soils.
-The ice machine in the lobby is observed with mold growth on the plastic tube that directs the ice while it’s being dispensed. 
Ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current build-up and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. PIC corrected these violations during the inspection and so no follow-up is being issued.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: The back entrance to the facility has visible light gaps present when the door is closed. These gaps may allow for the entrance of insects and other pests. The current rubber seal is observed damaged and in need of being replaced. Ensure repairs are made to protect the outer opening of the establishment from the entry of insects and rodents.
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: At the start of the inspection, there was no sanitizer bucket available. A sanitizer bucket was made during today’s inspection and tested from the dispenser at the triple sink and tested at 150ppm QUAT. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is made, tested, and readily available during all hours of operation. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The soda dispensers at the drive-thru were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. Remove the soda nozzles and perform a wash rinse sanitize cycle to remove any residue or soil. Ensure this process is completed a t a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residue. 
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
